title: WPMS/1193/2017 of Om Prakash Saini AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1193 of 2017
Om Prakash Saini & another .........Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ........Respondents
Present:- Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent nos. 1 to 3.
Mr. Ankur Sharma, Mr. Shantanu Bhardwaj, Advocates for the caveator.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 This petition has been filed by the petitioners who claim
to be the life Members of a Society, which runs a school.
2. This petition has not been filed by the Society nor the
Society has been made a party.
3. An individual member of a Society (which is a registered
Society under the Societies Registration Act) has challenged the order
of the State Government (dated 04.01.2017), by which the school
which was being run by the Society, is now to be provincialized. The
petitioners are against the provincialisation, and hence, challenged
this impugned order dated 04.01.2017 before this Court.
4. A preliminary objection has been raised at the hands of
the caveator that this writ petition is not maintainable at the hands of
the Members of the Society, particularly when there is no resolution
of the Society in this regard.
5. Learned counsel for the caveator has also relied upon a
decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of U.P. and
another Vs. C.O.D. Chheoki Employees' Cooperative Society
Limited and others, reported in (1997) 3 SCC 681, wherein the
Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under:

2
"A member of the society has no independent right qua
the society and it is the society that is entitled to
represent as the corporate aggregate. No individual
member is entitled to assail the constitutionality of the
provisions of the Act, rules and the bye-laws as he has
his right under the Act, rules and the bye-laws and is
subject to its operation. The stream cannot rise higher
than the source."
6. The objection raised before this Court appears to be
valid. This writ petition is not maintainable at the hands of an
individual member of a society, particularly when there is no
resolution of the society in this regard.
7. In view of the aforesaid, the writ petition has no merit
and the same is dismissed in limine.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 18.05.2017
Ankit/
